items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (mergeQueryStates, restorePersistedQuery, retrievePersistedQuery) and JSDoc covers the public helper and the merge. The RestoredError control flow is non-obvious but has a comment ('reject without dispatching a new error'). Formatting was fixed with prettier.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The marker lives in query.ts rather than a separate persister.ts module. Query#restore calls this.setState(state) instead of a dedicated reducer action. It uses an exception class (RestoredError) for control flow, the public type has `PersisterRestoreResult<any, any>` and the test needs an `as any` cast. Bulk restore doesn't share the Query restore path.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Persisted state is not normalised: `state: Partial<QueryState>` is spread directly into the query state with no check of counts or timestamps. Status is only derived when undefined. Errors are not swallowed, and fetchStatus and fetchMeta are reset to idle/null.

items.name: Restore path API contract
items.name_zh: 恢复路径 API 约定
items.evidence: createPersisterRestoreResult is exported and uses a Symbol marker, and success callbacks are skipped (tested). It applies state with setState rather than a dedicated action, and bulk restoreQueries uses queryCache.build/setState plus mergeQueryStates rather than the shared marker restore path.

items.name: Existing persister contract preserved
items.name_zh: 保持既有 persister 约定
items.evidence: The plain-data branch in fetch is unchanged (`const data = result as TData`). New exports are additive, and the QueryPersister return type is only widened. experimental_createQueryPersister options are unchanged and retrieveQuery is kept. All P2P tests pass.
